Phase 1 RCA (rebar-debug): CONFIRMED DEFECT. MCP 1.29.0 defines generic `mcp.server.fastmcp.server.Settings` before `FastMCP` under postponed annotations, so `Settings.model_fields["lifespan"]` remains `_complete=False` with `ForwardRef("Callable[[FastMCP[LifespanResultT]], AbstractAsyncContextManager[LifespanResultT]] | None")`. The module never rebuilds the model after `FastMCP` becomes available. On the first `FastMCP()` construction, pydantic-settings 2.15 `DefaultSettingsSource` inspects that incomplete field and emits `IncompleteFieldDefinitionWarning`; with the warning promoted to error, public `build_server()` aborts at `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:627` before construction completes.

Discriminating proof: (1) direct upstream-only `FastMCP("direct")` reproduces in a fresh process without importing rebar, ruling out rebar config/tool/schema and Starlette integration; (2) fresh-process state is model=False/field=False before construction, first construction emits exactly one warning and auto-completes the model, second construction emits zero; (3) pre-calling public Pydantic `Settings.model_rebuild()` returns True, resolves the annotation, and makes the first construction warning-free; (4) holding MCP 1.29.0/Pydantic 2.13.4 fixed, both pydantic-settings 2.14.2 and 2.15.0 begin with the same unresolved model, while only 2.15 warns—commit 57d192544c exposed a pre-existing MCP defect rather than creating it; (5) untreated-success versus pre-rebuilt rebar construction produced identical host/port/lifespan values, identical default lifespan context `{}`, 61 tools, and identical serialized tool-schema SHA-256 b516757c10ab635d84b3b6345f7096973e25f0dc598c5e7b58bee935661ca70e. Upstream modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk#3294 confirms the exact v1 defect and endorses `Settings.model_rebuild()` after import as the one-line workaround; v1 is critical-fixes-only.

Defect legitimacy: pydantic-settings sources/utils.py:32-53 defines incomplete FieldInfo as unsafe for settings-source inspection and warns it may silently fail to resolve values; rebar supports MCP 1.x and publishes `rebar-mcp`. Caller-dependency gate: expected post-fix is only complete Settings metadata plus no warning before first rebar server construction. `build_server()` callers consume the returned FastMCP server; no caller inspects or depends on the warning/incomplete metadata, and runtime/schema/lifecycle parity is proven above. Direct upstream FastMCP consumers outside rebar’s factory are unaffected. Safe to enter Phase 2 with a local constructor-boundary compatibility rebuild; no dependency, lifecycle, startup, tool, or schema behavior change.

Proof: direct upstream FastMCP reproduced without rebar; first versus second construction isolated process-global completion; pre-calling public Settings.model_rebuild returned True and removed the warning; dependency A/B and upstream issue 3294 ruled out rebar config, schemas, Starlette, and a new pydantic defect. Fix: build_server lazily imports MCP v1 Settings beside FastMCP and calls Settings.model_rebuild before either HTTP or stdio construction; docs/env-vars.md was mechanically regenerated for the shifted source-line citation. Scope and safety: caller sweep found no consumer that depends on incomplete metadata or the warning; all rebar construction routes through build_server. The fix restores metadata completeness, adds no dependency or capability, preserves optional imports, and weakens no test. Validation: original warning-as-error node 1 passed; output-schema module 36 passed; stdio plus real HTTP lifecycle 2 passed; fresh-process original report exits 0 and prints rebar; make lint and make typecheck pass; full make test exits 0 with 13536 passed, 52 skipped, 289 deselected. Siblings: no second production FastMCP constructor; one direct constructor is test-only and excluded from the production construct sweep. Parity rule is that every rebar MCP server construction completes upstream Settings metadata before first stdio or HTTP construction; CLI, public facade, MCP tools, and automated callers all route through build_server; dual-direction is N/A. Residual warnings already owned: stumpy-cinnabar-basenji, treelike-unamusing-grosbeak, dragonish-sylphic-sheep, and unamicable-exuberant-chupacabra; accepted out of this fix with no duplicates. ## Context
The supported public `rebar.mcp_server.build_server()` path emits `pydantic_settings.sources.utils.IncompleteFieldDefinitionWarning` on its first FastMCP construction under the locked MCP 1.29.0 / pydantic-settings 2.15.0 dependency pair. Promoting the warning to an error aborts MCP startup.

## Confirmed Root Cause
MCP v1 defines generic `mcp.server.fastmcp.server.Settings` before `FastMCP` while postponed annotations are enabled. Its `lifespan` field remains an unresolved `ForwardRef` and the upstream module never calls `Settings.model_rebuild()` after `FastMCP` is defined. Pydantic-settings 2.15 intentionally detects this unsafe incomplete field when settings sources inspect it. Direct upstream `FastMCP("direct")` reproduces without rebar; the 2.14.2/2.15.0 A/B proves 2.15 exposed a pre-existing MCP defect. Upstream issue modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk#3294 confirms the mechanism and endorses an after-import `Settings.model_rebuild()` workaround because MCP v1 is critical-fixes-only.

## Repair Plan
1. At rebar’s existing lazy MCP import boundary in `build_server()`, import the MCP v1 Settings model and invoke its public Pydantic `model_rebuild()` before either stdio or HTTP FastMCP construction. Keep the compatibility action inside the optional-dependency boundary; do not make MCP a core import.
2. Do not suppress the warning, pin/downgrade dependencies, change MCP transport configuration, or migrate to MCP v2. This repair resolves the incomplete model metadata while preserving all settings values, lifecycle callbacks/contexts, tool registrations, and input/output schemas.
3. Add a fresh-subprocess facade contract test. A subprocess is required because a successful first FastMCP construction auto-completes the process-global model and could mask the defect in an in-process suite. The subprocess promotes exactly `IncompleteFieldDefinitionWarning` to an error, calls public `build_server()`, and asserts successful construction of the named `rebar` server.
4. Verify the focused warning-as-error oracle, the complete MCP output-schema coverage module, stdio construction, real Streamable-HTTP initialize/lifespan behavior, lint, and typecheck.

## Test Contract Card
- authoritative_contract: pydantic-settings 2.15 defines incomplete FieldInfo as unsafe for settings-source inspection and prescribes `model_rebuild()`; rebar publishes `rebar-mcp`/`build_server()` over the supported MCP v1 range.
- trigger_preconditions: a fresh Python interpreter, the supported MCP extra, and the exact warning category promoted to error before the first public server construction.
- production_path: subprocess -> `rebar.mcp_server.build_server()` -> MCP `FastMCP.__init__` -> `Settings` sources.
- test_tier: subprocess facade contract; an in-process unit is insufficient because first construction mutates global model completeness.
- observable_postcondition: subprocess exits 0 and reports the constructed server name `rebar`; no warning suppression is permitted.
- ci_gate: focused pytest node plus the repository `make test` gate.
- negative_control: omitted as a genuinely single first-construction defect; existing normal stdio and real HTTP lifecycle tests are the behavior-preservation controls.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The exact MCP v1 owning model and unresolved `lifespan` annotation remain documented in the ticket RCA with discriminating runtime evidence.
- [ ] A fresh-process public `build_server()` call succeeds with `IncompleteFieldDefinitionWarning` promoted to an error.
- [ ] The repair completes the upstream Settings model rather than suppressing the warning or downgrading/pinning pydantic-settings.
- [ ] MCP remains an optional lazy import and no dependency is added.
- [ ] Existing stdio construction, Streamable-HTTP initialize/lifespan behavior, and the full MCP output-schema coverage module remain green.
- [ ] Lint and typecheck pass.

## Verification
- `pytest -q tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_settings_completion.py`
- `pytest -q tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py`
- `pytest -q tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py::test_build_server_default_is_stdio_fastmcp tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py::test_http_transport_boots_and_serves_initialize`
- `make lint`
- `make typecheck`
